title: Scraper: HPE ProLiant AMD (SPP package, hardest)
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Scraper for HPE ProLiant DL/Apollo AMD servers. Hardest of the server-vendor scrapers — HPE distributes BIOS only as part of large multi-component **Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP)** ISOs gated behind My HPE Hewlett Packard Enterprise Support Center login.

board_class: EPYC.

HPE EPYC ProLiant lineup:
- Rome/Milan: DL325 Gen10 / Gen10 Plus, DL345 Gen10 Plus, DL385 Gen10 / Gen10 Plus, DL725, DL765 Gen11
- Genoa: DL345 Gen11, DL365 Gen11, DL385 Gen11, DL325 Gen11
- Apollo: XL225n, XL345 Gen10/Gen11

Why this is hard:
- SPP ISO is 5–8 GB; BIOS component is buried inside as a single .scexe (HP self-extracting executable) within the ISO's root /firmware-* tree.
- HPE Support Center requires **HPE Passport login** for current SPPs. Old SPP ISOs are sometimes archived on archive.org.
- HPE also publishes individual .scexe BIOS components on https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/swd/ but these typically also require login auth tokens.

Possible strategies (in priority order):
1. **archive.org Wayback CDX** for support.hpe.com/.../*.scexe URLs that were public before login walls expanded. Same pattern as AsRock/MSI; coverage will be partial and historical only.
2. **vendor-supplied SDR**: HPE publishes Service Definition Repository metadata on https://downloads.linux.hpe.com/SDR/ for ISO/MCP/SPP — sometimes with downloadable per-component .scexe files. Worth investigating.
3. **Skip HPE entirely for now** and document as unsupported.

Unwrapping:
- HPE .scexe → standard zlib+executable wrapper. After unwrap, the BIOS payload is still a vendor-specific ROM-image format; recover the raw flash image via tools from BIOSUtilities (MIT) or manual extraction.

License-safe references: nothing relevant in surveyed prior art.

Acceptance criteria:
- Class at src/psp_etl/scrape/hpe.py — even if it's a stub that documents 'no public access without login' until strategy (1) or (2) is proven viable
- If (1) Wayback path works: at least one fixture ISO/SCExe parsed end-to-end
- classify_board_class returns EPYC for SP3/SP5 (already wired)
- CLI registration

Note: this issue is intentionally low priority. If vendor-corpus completeness is goal, prioritise Supermicro/Gigabyte-server/ASRock-Rack/ASUS-server first.

Related: #79, #81.
